original_question: Find the asymptotic value of Dcurves(m,n), the minimum number of distinct distances between m points on one constant-degree algebraic curve and n points on another when the curves avoid the exceptional cases of containing parallel lines, orthogonal lines, or concentric circles.
target_in_paper: Section 5, Problem 17: "Find the asymptotic value of Dcurves(m, n)." (page 8). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
correct_elements: You correctly identified the bipartite two-curve distinct-distances problem, used the paper's notation Dcurves(m, n), asked for the asymptotic value rather than a one-off bound, and listed exactly the three exceptional configurations named in the paper: parallel lines, orthogonal lines, and concentric circles. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
missing_details: The ambient setting should be made explicit: the problem is in the real Euclidean plane R^2, and the quantity being counted is the bipartite distance set {|p-q| : p in P1, q in P2}, not distances within P1 or within P2. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1406.1949))

Dcurves(m, n) is a minimum over all admissible choices of curves gamma1, gamma2 and point sets P1 subset gamma1, P2 subset gamma2 with |P1|=m and |P2|=n; your draft reads a bit like the curves might already be fixed. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1406.1949))

The exceptional-case exclusion should be unpacked in cross-curve form: there is no line L1 contained in gamma1 and line L2 contained in gamma2 with L1 parallel to L2 or L1 orthogonal to L2, and no circles C1 contained in gamma1 and C2 contained in gamma2 that are concentric. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
The asymptotic regime is in the two variables m and n; Section 5 adopts the usual bipartite convention m<=n without loss of generality. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1406.1949))

To stay paper-faithful, the question should be framed as the open problem of determining the full asymptotic growth, not as re-deriving the currently known lower bound, since the Pach-de Zeeuw bound is stated immediately before Problem 17. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
refined_question: For integers 1<=m<=n, let Dcurves(m, n) be the minimum possible cardinality of the bipartite Euclidean distance set {|p-q| : p in P1, q in P2}, taken over all finite sets P1 subset gamma1 and P2 subset gamma2 with |P1|=m and |P2|=n, where gamma1,gamma2 subset R^2 are constant-degree algebraic curves such that there is no line L1 subset gamma1 and line L2 subset gamma2 with L1 parallel to L2 or L1 orthogonal to L2, and no circles C1 subset gamma1 and C2 subset gamma2 that are concentric. Determine the asymptotic growth of Dcurves(m, n) as a function of m and n.
justification: The draft is targeting the survey's open Problem 17, not the lower-bound theorem itself. In Section 5, the paper first defines bipartite distance counts D(P1, P2), then the unrestricted minimum D(m, n), and then the curve-restricted quantity Dcurves(m, n) for point sets on algebraic curves, with exactly the three exceptional configurations named in your draft. The very next sentence records the known Pach-de Zeeuw lower bound Dcurves(m, n)=Omega(min{m^{2/3}n^{2/3}, m^2, n^2}), and the paper then states Problem 17: determine the asymptotic value of Dcurves(m, n). So the sharp paper-faithful refinement is simply to make the definition of Dcurves(m, n) fully explicit and self-contained, without broadening it beyond the survey's formulation. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
